properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 6 at 5:38AM PST until November 7 at 12:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Waves can run up significantly farther on a beach
than normal, including over rocks and jetties. Sneaker waves
can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull
them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or
drowning.

the water, especially those who will be razor clamming. Keep
children and pets away from the surf zone. Keep off of
jetties, rocks and logs near the surf zone. If you see someone
swept into the sea do not swim in after them. Call 911 and
keep an eye on them until help arrives.

Tropical Depression 31W. As of 7:00 PM ChST this evening, 31W was
moving northwest at 21 MPH with maximum sustained winds of 30 MPH.
The current track shows 31W passing north of Agrihan early Saturday
morning, strengthening into a low-end tropical storm. However,
tropical storm-force winds are expected to remain north of the
center, so damaging winds are not expected for Alamagan, Pagan,
or Agrihan at this time. However, residents of the northern CNMI
should monitor the forecast for any changes to this expectation.
31W is forecast to exit the northern CNMI by Saturday afternoon,
possibly remaining a tropical storm.

Through tonight, prepare for increasing rainfall, with isolated
thunderstorms and strong gusty winds within the heavier showers. 1
to 2 inches of rainfall are expected, with gusts up to 40 mph
possible.

This will be the final Special Weather Statement issued regarding TD
31W. Please refer to NWS Guam Public Advisories under WMO header
WTPQ31 PGTW, as well as JTWC bulletins under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW
and WTPN31 PGTW.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 6 at 3:18PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
A developing tropical disturbance, Invest 99W, is quickly approaching
the islands of the northern CNMI. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center
(JTWC) has issued a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA) for 99W.
This means that development into a significant tropical cyclone is
likely within the next 24 hours. What this means for the northern
CNMI of Alamagan, Pagan and Agrihan is that you can expect an
increase in showers and thunderstorms with strong gusty winds as 99W
moves past. Invest 99W is currently not expected to move through the
northern CNMI stronger than a Tropical Depression. However, as with
all tropical cyclones, this could change.

Invest 99W is currently moving fairly quickly, which is a good thing
for the northern CNMI. At the current speed, 99W looks to pass
through the region near Alamagan Saturday morning or early afternoon,
not becoming a Tropical Storm until later in the day, west of the
islands. Invest 99W will be monitored over the next 24 hours for any
significant changes in expectations and the residents of the
northern CNMI should continue to monitor forecasts for any changes to
the current expectations. For now, prepare for increasing rainfall,
with isolated thunderstorms and strong gusty winds within the heavier
showers. Only 1 to 2 inches of rainfall is expected, with gusts up
to 40 mph possible.

For more information on Invest 99W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.
